_schema: mchatai-source/personas/_verbs.json — GENERATED by verbs/build_index.py from verbs/ios/*.json (Phase AV.0); edit the verb files, never this one. The same list rides inside personas/_index.json so one fetch serves the chat. Design: mchatai_macOS/docs/IOS_AGENT_SKILLS_PLAN.md.

verbs.example: Write that up as a document in AI Write
verbs.summary: Writes a new document into the AI Write app on this device with a title and Markdown text, and returns a link that opens it.
verbs.title: Create a document in AI Write
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person wants something written up, saved or kept. Put the whole text in one call.

arguments.name: script
arguments.description: 250 to 400 words of plain spoken sentences

verbs.example: Turn that write-up into a short podcast
verbs.summary: Reads a script aloud with the system voice and saves it as an episode in the Podcasts library on this device, with a link that plays it.
verbs.title: Make a podcast episode
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person wants to listen rather than read. Write the script first: 250 to 400 words of plain spoken sentences, no headings or Markdown.

arguments.name: url
arguments.description: The PDF's address, such as https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.15285

verbs.example: Read the PDF at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.15285 and summarize its method
verbs.summary: Downloads a PDF and returns its text page by page; scanned pages are read with on-device OCR.
verbs.title: Read a PDF
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person points at a PDF (a paper's full text, a report, a form) and wants what is in it.

arguments.name: document
arguments.description: The document's id, or words from its title

verbs.example: Make a podcast from my document about local language models
verbs.summary: Reads an AI Write document, turns it into a 250 to 400 word spoken script with the on-device model, and saves the script as a podcast episode. A fixed chain: no planner decides anything.
verbs.title: Podcast from a document
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person wants to listen to something they already have in AI Write.

arguments.name: ref
arguments.description: The document's id, or words from its title

verbs.example: Open my notes on local language models and read me the main point
verbs.summary: Returns an AI Write document's title and text by its id or title. When no document matches, it lists the closest titles so the person can pick.
verbs.title: Read a document from AI Write
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person refers to something they wrote or saved earlier ('my notes on…', 'the write-up from yesterday').

arguments.name: url
arguments.description: The full address, starting with http:// or https://

verbs.example: Read https://example.com/post and tell me the three main points
verbs.summary: Loads a web address and returns the page's title and visible text, so the agent can quote, summarize or write about it. A PDF address is read as a PDF.
verbs.title: Read a web page
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person gives an address or a search returned one, and the words on that page matter.

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: The id from the search, such as 2410.15285 (arXiv) or the item's address

arguments.name: source
arguments.description: The source the id came from; leave empty when it is the same as the search

verbs.example: Read paper 2410.15285 and tell me what it found
verbs.summary: Fetches one item's title, authors, date, abstract and link by the id a search returned, from the source it came from.
verbs.title: Read a paper
verbs.whenToUse: Use after a search, on the single best match: the one whose title and abstract are really about the topic, not the first result.

arguments.name: query
arguments.description: Search words, such as 'on-device language models iPhone'

arguments.name: source
arguments.description: Which source to search: one of the ids this agent lists, such as arxiv or semanticscholar. Leave empty for the agent's first source.

verbs.example: Find a recent paper about speech recognition on phones
verbs.summary: Searches a research source for items on a topic and lists up to eight with their id, year and a line of summary. The source is arXiv unless the agent or the person names another (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed, Hacker News, or a site from My sources).
verbs.title: Search a research source
verbs.whenToUse: Use first when the person wants a paper, a study or a post on a topic. Pick the source that fits the topic when more than one is offered.

verbs.example: Summarize this page into AI Write
verbs.summary: Reads a web page, summarizes it with the on-device model, and saves the summary with the page's address as a new AI Write document. A fixed chain: no planner decides anything.
verbs.title: Summarize a page into AI Write
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person wants to keep the gist of a page they are reading.

arguments.name: style
arguments.description: notes, paragraph or script (a spoken script in plain sentences)

arguments.name: maxWords
arguments.description: The longest the summary may be, in words; 150 when empty

verbs.example: Summarize this in five bullet points
verbs.summary: Summarizes text with the on-device model, in the style asked for (short notes, one paragraph, or a spoken script) and within a word budget.
verbs.title: Summarize text
verbs.whenToUse: Use when text from a page, a PDF, a document or a transcript is longer than what the person asked for.

arguments.name: file
arguments.description: The recording the person picked (a file on this device)

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: The language spoken, such as en-US or es-ES; the device's language when empty

verbs.example: Transcribe this recording and save the text to AI Write
verbs.summary: Writes down the words in an audio file on this device with Apple's on-device speech model.
verbs.title: Transcribe a recording
verbs.whenToUse: Use when the person has a recording (a voice memo, an interview, a lecture) and wants its words.
